bank_name: <the bank's name as the agent should say it>
opening_sentence: <the exact first sentence(s) the brief requires: who is calling and that the call is recorded, if required>
confirm_question: <the exact question that confirms the right person; keep the placeholders {title} and {last_name}>

confirmation.max_asks: <integer: how many times the question may be asked in total>

forbidden_before_verification: <words or topics that may not be said before identity is verified>
robot_answer: <what to say if asked whether the caller is a robot or an AI, as an instruction>
scam_answer: <what to say if asked whether this is a scam, as an instruction>

third_party.instructions: <the brief's rules when someone other than the customer answers, in full>
third_party.deceased_sentence: <the exact sentence to say when told the customer has died, if the brief gives one>

days: <which days a callback may be booked on, as tokens from: today, next_business_day>
callback.max_asks: <integer: how many times to ask for another time when the offered one is outside the window>

questions.field: <field name exactly as in the tool API enum>
questions.format: <format the tool needs, in words, plus any parsing rule from the brief>

identity.max_wrong_total: <integer: wrong answers in total that end the check>
identity.on_wrong: <what to do after a wrong answer, as an instruction: repeat the same question, or move on, as the brief says>
identity.numeric_date_order: <how a date given only as numbers is read: day_month_year or month_day_year>
identity.hint_value: <value of the tool's hint field that the brief gives a rule for (from the API file), or empty>
identity.hint_instruction: <what to do when that hint is returned, as an instruction, or empty>
identity.decline_rule: <the brief's rule when the customer does not want to answer, in full>
identity.on_fail_sentence: <what to tell a customer who failed the check, as a sentence to say>

debt_intro_sentence: <the exact sentence to say once verified that states who is calling and why, as the agent should say it; the product, amount and days late are added after it>

product_words.<product type value from the API file>: <words to use for it; may contain {card_last4} or another field of the product>

floor_field.<product type value>: <field of the product that holds the minimum amount, when the brief defines the minimum as a field of the product>

floor_fraction: <the minimum a customer may offer as a fraction of the past-due amount, for example 0.5, when the brief defines it that way; else empty>

bands.name: <band name>
bands.deadline_business_days: <integer: the nth business day after today>

date_adjust.non_business_day: <what to do when the customer names a weekend day or holiday: next_business_day, previous_business_day, or none>
date_adjust.after_deadline: <what to do when the customer names a date after the latest allowed date: offer_deadline, or none>

attempt1_rule.rule: <which date the first persuasion attempt proposes, one of: last_business_day_of_week (of next week when today is that day), next_business_day, nth_business_day, deadline, none>

attempt2_rule.date: <which date the second persuasion attempt proposes, one of: deadline, next_business_day, nth_business_day, last_business_day_of_week; deadline when the brief says the latest allowed date>
attempt2_rule.amount: <what the second attempt proposes: floor or full>
attempt2_rule.text: <the brief's own words for attempt 2, or empty>

date_rules: <every rule about promise dates, in full, as instructions: validity, weekend or holiday handling, vague periods, this/next weekday, dates after the latest allowed date>
amount_rules: <every rule about amounts, in full: what to ask first, the floor, offers above or below it, what may never be asked>
persuasion_rules: <every rule about refusals and persuasion attempts, in full: what counts as a refusal, what each attempt proposes, what to do when attempts are used up>
special_rules: <every rule for special situations, in full: hardship, already paid, dispute, does not want to talk, unknown information, and which rule comes first>
recording_rules: <every rule about the read-back, changes at the read-back, one promise per product, changing a recorded promise, and failed recordings>

sentences.first_ask_multi: <the exact first question when there are several products, or empty>
sentences.confirm_question: <the exact confirmation question at the read-back>
sentences.after_promise: <the exact sentence to say after a recorded promise>
sentences.debt_line: <the sentence that states one late product, with the placeholders {product}, {amount} and {days_late}, in the call's language, always filled: the brief's exact sentence when it gives one, else one composed from the brief's own wording; the amount is a bare number, so write the currency word around it>

transfers.when: <in which situation to transfer, as an instruction, including anything to say or ask first>

unclear.outcome: <close_call outcome when the right person could not be confirmed>

end_reasons.key: <short snake_case key; use refused, hardship, dispute, paid, service_error when the brief has these situations, and add others the brief defines>
end_reasons.meaning: <when a verified call ends this way without a promise, for the agent>
end_reasons.note_reason: <add_note reason value for a product ending this way, or empty>

multi_product.enabled: <true when customers can have several late products>
multi_product.rules: <every rule for several products, in full, or empty>

verify_identity.field: <request field that names the security question>
verify_identity.hint: <response field with a hint, or empty>

get_account.products: <response field with the list of products>

goodbye: <a closing sentence that thanks the customer and says goodbye>
ambiguities: <anything the briefs leave unclear or contradictory, and how you resolved it; empty list if nothing>

rules.section: <one of: opening, third_party, identity, debt, dates, amounts, promise, recording, other, closing, multi>
